docs.title: Cobblemon mods by shiero
docs.text:
Mods that turn a Cobblemon world into an adventure: roads and towns worth exploring, a Nuzlocke that enforces itself, every HM in your own hands, and more. The documentation for all of them lives here.

Browse the mods Report a bug Discord

docs.title: The mods
docs.text:
All Client-only No Cobblemon

Routes Roads between your structures, named routes and map integration. No Cobblemon

Cobblemon Nuzlocke & Soul Link A Hardcore Nuzlocke the game enforces, plus co-op Soul Link. Cobblemon 1.7–1.8 Needs Routes

Cobblemon Picnic A picnic table that re-rolls the wild spawns around it. Cobblemon 1.8+

Cobblemon HMs Your Pokémon lend you their moves: HMs on your fist, auras on you. Cobblemon 1.8+

Cobblemon Raid Icons Every raid den on your minimap and world map. Client-only Needs Raid Dens

Cobblemon Champions Training Stat points instead of EVs, spent from the summary. Cobblemon 1.8

Cobblemon Mid-Battle EXP EXP at every knockout, used in the same battle. Cobblemon 1.7–1.8

Tree Carve Carve messages and symbols into logs with a sword. MC 1.21.1 · 26.1–26.3 No Cobblemon

Cobblemon PokeTowns Pokémon Centers, Marts and gyms in your villages. Not released yet Cobblemon 1.8+ Needs CobbleDollars + Waystones

Cobblemon Action Combat Cobblemon battles in real time: you drive your Pokémon. Not released yet Cobblemon 1.8+

docs.title: Compatibility
docs.text:
Every mod runs on Minecraft 1.21.1, on Fabric and NeoForge; Tree Carve also has jars for 26.1 to 26.3. Both means the server and every player's game. Each mod's home page ends with the full list for your loader.

docs.title: Installing
docs.text:
Every mod runs on Minecraft 1.21.1 on either Fabric or NeoForge. Drop the jar for your loader into mods/ — never both jars at once.

Which Cobblemon each mod runs on, and what else it needs, is in the compatibility table above. Each mod's home page ends with the full list for your loader.

docs.title: Configuring
docs.text:
Routes and Nuzlocke are set up on the world-creation screen and stored with that world. Picnic, Cobblemon HMs and Raid Icons use in-game config: a command, or a settings screen. Tree Carve is set by operators with /treecarve config. Mid-Battle EXP has nothing to configure.

See each mod's Configuration page.

docs.title: Finding things
docs.text:
Every section follows the same order: Getting Started, the mod's own feature pages, Commands, Configuration, Troubleshooting, Community Credits.

The search box at the top covers every mod at once.

docs.title: Found a bug, or have an idea?
docs.text:
Post in #mod-tickets on Discord and tag it — Bug, Crash, Idea or Feedback. A bot files it as an issue, replies in your thread with what it needs from you, and posts back there when it is closed. You do not need a GitHub account.

For a crash, attach crash-reports/crash-*.txt — the stack trace is what turns a hunt into a fix.

Something wrong on a page? Say so in the Discord — same place, same thread, and it gets fixed here.

docs.title: 📜 License
docs.text:
Every mod shiero publishes ships under the same license — every mod documented in this wiki carries the identical LICENSE file, word for word, and it ships inside the jar so you always have a copy. The short version: if you make money, shiero makes money. That file is the binding document; this page is the friendly summary.

What you are doing Where you stand 🎮 Playing — solo, or on a server that does not charge ✅ Free 📦 Putting it in a free modpack ✅ Free — keep the license and attribution intact 🎥 Videos, streams, reviews — monetized included ✅ Free — credit the mod and link a project page 💰 Anything that earns money off the mod itself 🤝 Ask first — a written agreement with a revenue share

Monetized videos and the donations your content brings in are not commercial use of the mod. Content creation is free here.

docs.title: 💬 One way to reach the author
docs.text: Everything the license asks you to arrange happens in the Discord. There is no contact email — the server is the only channel, and it is where agreements get sorted out fastest.

docs.title: 🎥 Creators: yes, and monetized is fine
docs.text:
Make videos, stream it, review it, write guides — all free, all encouraged, including monetized content (ads, sponsorships, donations, memberships, even patron-exclusive series). No agreement, no revenue share. The only ask: credit the mod and link an official page in your description.

docs.text: Use it, copy it, modify it, share it — free of charge. Redistributing it for free, including inside a free modpack, is explicitly allowed. Every copy and derivative has to keep the license file and clear attribution to the original project.

docs.title: 💰 Revenue-share: commercial use
docs.text:
Anything that makes money off the software itself needs a written agreement with the author first: selling the mod or derivatives, charging for access, downloads or hosting, bundling it in a paid modpack, server, product or service, paid ranks or perks tied to it, or monetized distribution. The agreement includes an agreed share of that revenue. (Content creation is exempt — see above.)

Get in touch before any commercial use, in the Discord.

docs.title: 🏷️ Attribution
docs.text: All copies and derivative works must credit the mod and its author, shiero, and link back to an official project page.

The software is provided as is, without warranty of any kind, express or implied. The author is not liable for any damages arising from its use — see the LICENSE file for the exact terms.

Not sure which side you're on?

Playing on a private server with friends, or handing the pack to them for free: free. Charging players, donations-for-perks tied to the mod, or a paid pack that includes it: ask in the Discord first — agreements are friendly and quick, and the answer is usually yes.

docs.title: 🐛 Reporting bugs & ideas
docs.text:
Found a bug, or have an idea? Post it in the Discord — that is the whole process. You do not need a GitHub account. A bot turns your post into a tracked issue, replies in your thread with what it needs from you, and posts back there when it is closed.

One page for every mod: the process is identical, and the mod-specific detail is in the tabs below.

  1. You open a post in #mod-tickets and pick two tags: the mod and the type.
  2. The bot reads it within ~10 minutes and files a tracked issue, labelled from your tag.
  3. The bot replies in your thread saying what it still needs from you, if anything.
  4. shiero fixes it in a release.
  5. The bot posts back in your thread when the issue closes. 🎉

docs.title: Pick the right tag
docs.text:
The mod tag sends the report to the right place. The type tag decides how it is handled — and what the bot asks you for. It is the one thing worth getting right.

Tag Use it when What the bot does 🚨 Crash the game closes, freezes or fails to start jumps the queue; asks for the crash report 🐛 Bug something works, but wrong asks for versions, loader and steps 💡 Idea you want something that does not exist yet files it as a feature request — no logs needed 💬 Feedback an impression, a balance opinion, a "this felt off" recorded; nothing else needed from you

docs.title: What makes a great report
docs.text:
• What you did, what you expected, and what happened instead.
  • The mod version, your loader (Fabric or NeoForge), and whether you are on a modpack.
  • If the game crashed: attach crash-reports/crash-*.txt, or logs/latest.log if there is no crash report. The stack trace is what turns a hunt into a fix.
  • A screenshot or a short clip, if it is something you can see.

A report that gets fixed fast

Placing a picnic table underwater near coral crashes the client. MC 1.21.1, Cobblemon 1.7.3, Picnic 1.26.0, Fabric. Happens every time; crash report attached.

docs.title: Where to find your logs
docs.text:
Both live in your game folder — the instance folder if you use a launcher with profiles:

  • logs/latest.log — the log of the last session. It is overwritten every launch, so grab it before starting the game again.
  • crash-reports/crash-<date>.txt — one file per crash, written only when the game crashes.
Launcher How to open the folder Modrinth App open the profile, then the ⋮ menu → Open folder CurseForge right-click the profile → Open Folder Prism Launcher select the instance → Folder Vanilla launcher %appdata%\.minecraft on Windows, ~/Library/Application Support/minecraft on macOS

Attach the file to your post. If it is too big, paste it on mclo.gs and share the link.

docs.title: Extra detail, per mod
docs.text:
RoutesNuzlocke & Soul LinkPicnicCobblemon HMsRaid IconsChampions TrainingTree CarveMid-Battle EXPPokeTowns
  • Where it happened: the zone name the mod showed you — a route, an area, a town, or the Wild.
  • Whether the world was generated with this version of Routes or an older one, since roads are baked in at worldgen.
  • For map problems: which map mod (Xaero's Minimap, World Map, JourneyMap) and its version.
  • Which rule misbehaved: one catch per zone, permadeath, nicknames, shiny clause, level caps, or a Soul Link pairing.
  • Where you were: the zone name the mod showed you.

  • For Soul Link: how many players were linked, and what each was doing at the time.

  • Your Routes version as well as the Nuzlocke one — this mod is an add-on and the two move together.

Zone problems are usually Routes problems

"One catch per zone" is defined against Routes' zone model — the routes, areas and towns it generates are the capture zones. If the zone itself looks wrong (missing, badly shaped, oddly named), that is a Routes report, not a Nuzlocke one.

  • Whether it was the re-roll, the social side (benches, shiny aura, care) or the trainer battles.
  • What was around the table: biome, other spawners, and whether a modpack tuned the spawn rules.
  • For furniture or model issues, which other furniture mods are installed.
  • Which HM, whether it was a partner HM, an aura or a mount toggle, and which Pokémon was lending it.

Cooldowns are configurable

Before reporting "this HM is too slow", check Configuration — every HM's cooldown and power is a server-side setting, so a modpack may have tuned it away from the defaults.

Suggesting a new HM? Those are the most common request, and plenty of the ones that shipped started that way. The ones that get built fastest describe: the Pokémon move it is based on, what it should do in Minecraft, and whether it feels like an active (press to use, costs hunger) or a toggle (passive, blocks part of your hunger bar).

  • The output of /raidicons report while aiming at the den that is misbehaving. It carries almost everything a report on this mod needs, and it goes to logs/latest.log too. (Plain /raidicons opens the settings screen.)
  • Which Xaero mods you have — the minimap, the world map, or both — and their versions.
  • Your Cobblemon Raid Dens version. The mod reads that mod's blocks by name, so a den it stops recognising is usually a Raid Dens update.

Icons fill in as you walk

The mod only sees dens in chunks your client has already been sent. A map that is not covered in markers after teleporting somewhere new is working correctly, not failing.

  • The output of /champions sp <slot> for the Pokémon involved. It shows whether the Pokémon is in training, its stat points, effort values and IVs, and its final stats.
  • What you pressed — Save, Train, Load, Store or Delete — and on which page of the summary.
  • Whether the server changed any settings: /champions config lists them all.

Stats look wrong?

A stat point is +1 to the stat at any level, applied before the nature. Compare with the numbers on Stat Points before reporting a formula bug.

  • Your Minecraft version (1.21.1, or which 26.x) and loader: the mod ships a jar for each.
  • What you carved and where: the block, the text or symbols, the font and the dye. For a face that looks wrong, the output of /treecarve who while looking at it (it needs operator level 2).
  • Whether the server changed any settings: /treecarve config lists them all.

Carvings gone after an update?

A world moved from Minecraft 1.21.1 to 26.x loses its carvings. That is a known limitation, not something to report.

  • The battle: wild, trainer or another player, single or double, and which Pokémon fought.
  • The battle log lines around the knockout: they show what each Pokémon was paid.
  • For the move screen: whether it opened, what you dragged, and whether the battle ended while it was open.
  • Your Cobblemon version (1.7 or 1.8) and any EXP setting changed in Cobblemon's config.

The amounts are Cobblemon's

The mod pays at each knockout what Cobblemon would pay at the end. If the amount looks off, check the settings on Getting Started first: a Lucky Egg, Exp. Share or a modpack multiplier changes it here too.

  • Which settlement: Village, Town or gym Town, and its coordinates (/locate gives them).
  • Whether the world was generated with this version of PokeTowns, since settlements are built as chunks generate.
  • Whether PokeTowns: Replace Vanilla Villages is on, and the spacing chosen on the PokeTowns tab.
  • For gym problems: whether the COBBLEVERSE datapack is installed, and its version.

docs.title: What happens next
docs.text:
Your post becomes an issue labelled from its tag, and the bot replies in the thread so you know it landed. When the issue is closed, it posts back there — saying whether it was fixed or closed without a change, because those are not the same thing and you deserve to know which.

Everyone who reports gets thanked on the mod's community credits page: Routes · Nuzlocke · Picnic · Cobblemon HMs · Raid Icons · Champions Training · Mid-Battle EXP. 💚
